findings.evidence: Quotient.lean:40 `variable (R : Type u) {A : Type v} [CommRing R] [Ring A] [Algebra R A]`; Quotient.lean:50-54 `smul_mem'` proof via `rw [Algebra.smul_def]; exact I.mul_mem_left _ _`; Quotient.lean:100-103 already works with `I.restrictScalars R`; Basic.lean:108-109 `derivationLieAlgebra` is defined for `[NonUnitalNonAssocRing A] [Module R A] [SMulCommClass R A A] [IsScalarTower R A A]`; Octonion/Derivation.lean:225-227 `derivation_apply_mem_imaginary`.
findings.fix: State `def stableDerivations (S : Submodule R A) : LieSubalgebra R (derivationLieAlgebra R A)` with carrier `{D | ∀ x ∈ S, (D : Module.End R A) x ∈ S}` at the `NonUnitalNonAssocRing` level (`smul_mem'` becomes `S.smul_mem r (hD x hx)`), move it and `mem_stableDerivations` out of the `[Ring A] [Algebra R A]` variable block, and in the `Quotient` section use `stableDerivations R (I.restrictScalars R)` (the quotient construction already passes `I.restrictScalars R` to `Submodule.mapQ`).
findings.issue: `stableDerivations` requires `[Ring A] [Algebra R A]` and an `Ideal A`, but neither associativity nor multiplicative closure of `I` is used: `zero_mem'`/`add_mem'`/`lie_mem'` use only additive closure, and `smul_mem'` has to detour through `Algebra.smul_def` + `mul_mem_left` precisely because the ideal is not presented as an `R`-submodule. The natural level, matching `derivationLieAlgebra` in `Basic.lean:108-109`, is the Lie subalgebra of derivations preserving an arbitrary `S : Submodule R A` over `[NonUnitalNonAssocRing A] [Module R A] [SMulCommClass R A A] [IsScalarTower R A A]`; the repo already has a non-associative instance (`Octonion.derivation_apply_mem_imaginary` says every derivation of `𝕆` lies in the stabilizer of `imaginary R`).

summary: The quotient descent sits at the right level (commutative base ring, arbitrary associative algebra, any two-sided ideal), but the stabilizer subalgebra `stableDerivations` is stated only for ideals of associative algebras although its definition and closure proofs use nothing beyond the `R`-submodule structure, and the repo already has a non-associative instance of the same notion.
